channel.title: Countertop Report
channel.description: Specification-led buying notes on air fryers and meat thermometers. No prices are shown here by design; every claim links to the listing it came from.

item.title: Basket or oven-style air fryer: what should you compare?
item.description: They share a name and almost nothing else. Six things to compare before you decide which shape belongs on your counter.

item.title: A no-hype checklist for comparing air fryer capacity
item.description: Quarts are the least comparable number on the box. Eight questions that get you to a real figure.

item.title: How to assess cleanup and counter-space trade-offs
item.description: The two costs nobody puts in the comparison table — and the ones that decide whether an appliance gets used or stored.

item.title: Questions to ask before buying a multi-function kitchen appliance
item.description: Multi-function usually means one function done well and five done adequately. How to tell which is which before you pay.

item.title: Chefman 6-Quart Dual Basket: Two baskets, two windows, one finish time.
item.description: Cooking a main and a side at different temperatures without owning two appliances.

item.title: Chefman TurboFry 8-Quart: One big square basket, four modes, honest cleanup.
item.description: Batch cooking for four to six people who want one large chamber and one thing to wash.

item.title: Emeril Lagasse 26QT French Door: An oven that happens to air fry.
item.description: Households that want one countertop box to replace a toaster oven and an air fryer basket.

item.title: ThermoMaven 1-Sec Instant Read: The cheap upgrade that fixes the guesswork.
item.description: Anyone who already owns an air fryer or oven and keeps overcooking protein.

item.title: CHEF iQ Sense (Gen3): Set it, walk away, get told when it is done.
item.description: Long cooks — smoking, roasting, rotisserie — where you cannot stand at the oven.
